source: De Jong (2009/2010) Cognitive load theory, educational research, and instructional design: some food for thought
finding: Core critique. Extraneous and germane load cannot always be told apart. The same activity (for example relating a graph to a formula) can be extraneous redundancy or germane deep processing.
numbers: Instr Sci 38:105-134. Worked example: reducing extraneous load by linear hypertext may remove germane example comparison (quoting Paas et al. 2004).
quote: Reducing extraneous load in these cases may therefore also remove the affordances for germane processes.
limits: Conceptual review, no new data. Argument is by examples from earlier studies.
agent_relevance: Do not label a prompt element extraneous or germane in advance. Its role depends on goal and reader (model).

source: De Jong (2009/2010) Cognitive load theory, educational research, and instructional design: some food for thought
finding: Additivity premise is shaky. Sweller et al. 1998 said intrinsic and extraneous load are additive, but De Jong argues intrinsic and germane load cannot be simply added.
numbers: Quotes Sweller et al. (1998, p.263) on additivity. Two readings: if intrinsic (material) and germane (process) are different kinds of thing, adding them is a category error; if both are processes they interact.
limits: Argument only; no test of additivity with data in this paper.
agent_relevance: Do not build a token-budget rule total load = sum of parts. Treat load types as interacting.

source: De Jong (2009/2010) Cognitive load theory, educational research, and instructional design: some food for thought
finding: Germane load is explained after the fact. If learners do better, the cause is called germane; if worse, overload. This makes the concept hard to falsify.
numbers: Also asks whether germane load can be too much. Cites Kalyuga (2007) that extra germane prompts may push load past working-memory limits.
limits: Interpretive critique.
agent_relevance: Caution: a claim that a prompt adds germane load needs an independent measure, not just a better score.

source: De Jong (2009/2010) Cognitive load theory, educational research, and instructional design: some food for thought
finding: Novice germane may be expert extraneous. The same activity changes label with expertise (links to expertise reversal, subfield 04).
numbers: Gives the example that extra activities help novices and become redundant for experts.
limits: Conceptual; supported by expertise-reversal data covered elsewhere.
agent_relevance: Scaffold strength should depend on how capable the model is on the task. A strong model may be hurt by extra scaffolding.

source: De Jong (2009/2010) Cognitive load theory, educational research, and instructional design: some food for thought
finding: Measurement critique: the single-item effort rating (Paas 1992) is called reliable and valid, but De Jong finds the evidence thin. High Cronbach alpha (.90 and .82) makes load look like a student trait, which conflicts with the theory that load depends on task x person.
numbers: Alphas .90 and .82 from two studies (Paas 1992; Paas and van Merrienboer 1994). No convergent, discriminant or predictive validity data found in the cited source.
limits: Reads the older validation papers; does not run new data.
agent_relevance: Self-reported or proxy load numbers in LLM work need real validation before use.

source: De Jong (2009/2010) Cognitive load theory, educational research, and instructional design: some food for thought
finding: Load measures often do not track instruction. De Jong lists about 14 studies with performance differences but no load differences, and some with load differences but no performance difference. In Paas 1992 itself there was no difference in invested effort during practice.
numbers: Lists Paas 1992, Stark 2002, Tabbers 2004, Lusk and Atkinson 2007, Hummel 2006, Fischer 2008, Wouters 2009, Kester and Kirschner 2009 and others for performance without load difference; Paas 2007 and Seufert 2007 for the reverse.
limits: Vote-count style; no effect sizes.
agent_relevance: Do not assume a better result proves lower load, or lower load proves a better result.

source: De Jong (2009/2010) Cognitive load theory, educational research, and instructional design: some food for thought
finding: The same one-item question is read differently in different studies. Seufert et al. (2007) found different load effects with the same set-up, speculated to be because people read the item as extraneous load in one study and as overall load in the other.
numbers: Seufert et al. 2007, two studies, same design, different outcomes on a one-item scale.
limits: Speculative interpretation by the original authors.
agent_relevance: Wording of any self-rated load question put to a model will shape the result.

source: Klepsch, Schmitz and Seufert (2017) Development and validation of two instruments measuring intrinsic, extraneous, and germane cognitive load
finding: Study 1: both informed raters (trained on the load types) and naive raters separated low and high load overall. But germane load in the naive rating failed: learners did not tell low from high germane tasks.
numbers: Study 1 N=97. Low vs high load: informed F(1,89)=293.32, eta2=.77; naive F(1,89)=199.96, eta2=.69; no difference between approaches F(1,89)=1.18, p=.28. Informed single-item alpha about .25 (expected). Naive alpha ICL .86, ECL .80, GCL .80.
quote: Learners failed to differentiate between theoretically predicted low and high levels of germane load.
limits: German-speaking students; naive germane items were rated very high even in low-germane tasks, so they were rewritten.
agent_relevance: Even people briefed on the theory can be fooled on germane load. An LLM judge asked to rate germane load is likely worse.

source: Klepsch, Schmitz and Seufert (2017) Development and validation of two instruments measuring intrinsic, extraneous, and germane cognitive load
finding: Study 2 (revised germane items): confirmatory factor analysis could not clearly choose between the 3-factor model and a 2-factor model where germane merges with intrinsic. Three factors were only slightly better.
numbers: Study 2 N=65 to 95 per task. One-factor model fit poorly: TLI .418, CFI .612, RMSEA .071, AIC 2185. The three-factor model (Model 2) and the productive-vs-unproductive model (Model 4) both fit well. Alpha ICL .81, ECL .86, GCL .67 (3 items) and .85 (2 items).
quote: the model with three types of load (Model 2) and the model with two types of load ... (Model 4) do not differ that much
limits: Fit table is garbled in extracted text, so exact Model 2 vs Model 4 values not recorded. Authors still prefer 3 factors on measurement grounds.
agent_relevance: Statistics do not settle whether germane is a separate load. Do not hang agent design on a three-way split.

source: Klepsch, Schmitz and Seufert (2017) Development and validation of two instruments measuring intrinsic, extraneous, and germane cognitive load
finding: Informed raters: the load ratings correlate only moderately with the single mental-effort item, so the sub-scales overlap with general effort.
numbers: Study 1 correlations with effort item: intrinsic r=.41 to .68 (tasks varying ICL); extraneous r=.32 to .60 (tasks varying ECL); germane r=.32 to .41; sum of three r=.32 to .69.
limits: Overlap with effort shows the sub-scales are not clean, as De Jong warned.
agent_relevance: Effort-like signals blend all load sources.

source: Klepsch, Schmitz and Seufert (2017) Development and validation of two instruments measuring intrinsic, extraneous, and germane cognitive load
finding: Authors admit that the labels matter less than the fact that all of these demands use working memory.
numbers: Argument in discussion of Study 2.
quote: However one likes to name them, we end up measuring three types of cognitive load.
limits: Authors built the 3-way instrument, so they are not neutral.

source: Krieglstein, Beege, Rey, Ginns, Krell and Schneider (2022) A systematic meta-analysis of the reliability and validity of subjective cognitive load questionnaires in experimental multimedia learning research
finding: Large meta-analysis of four 3-load questionnaires (Eysink 2009, Leppink 2013 and 2014, Klepsch 2017). Reliability is satisfactory, but the load types correlate in ways that go against the theory.
numbers: Records screened N=1193. Pooled alpha: Leppink 2013 ICL .845, ECL .759, GCL .909 (k=28, 30, 24); Klepsch ICL .776, ECL .798, GCL .734; Leppink 2014 ICL .851, ECL .788, GCL .806; Eysink ECL .740 (its ICL and GCL are single items).
limits: Multimedia-learning experiments only; student samples; subjective ratings.
agent_relevance: Measurement quality is fine; construct validity is the open problem.

source: Krieglstein, Beege, Rey, Ginns, Krell and Schneider (2022) A systematic meta-analysis of the reliability and validity of subjective cognitive load questionnaires in experimental multimedia learning research
finding: ICL and ECL correlate positively, medium to large, across questionnaires. This contradicts independent, additive load types.
numbers: Pooled r for ICL-ECL about .30 (Leppink 2013, k=25), about .35 (Klepsch, k=16), up to .53 for Eysink (k=9). ECL-GCL negative in all but Eysink (up to about -.33). Table columns were garbled in extraction, so values are approximate.
limits: Could be measurement overlap (learners cannot split them) or real interaction; the meta-analysis cannot tell which.
agent_relevance: Plausible: a poorly presented task feels harder. Fix presentation and fix difficulty may not be separate knobs.

source: Krieglstein, Beege, Rey, Ginns, Krell and Schneider (2022) A systematic meta-analysis of the reliability and validity of subjective cognitive load questionnaires in experimental multimedia learning research
finding: Criterion validity: ICL and ECL relate negatively to retention and transfer; GCL relates positively (small effects).
numbers: Klepsch: ICL-retention r=-.195, ECL-retention -.205, GCL-retention +.219; ECL-transfer -.261, GCL-transfer +.217. Leppink 2013: GCL-retention +.188, GCL-transfer +.173, ICL-transfer -.188.
limits: Correlational. Learners who learn well may simply report more germane effort afterwards.
agent_relevance: The germane rating predicts learning, but may be a retrospective proxy of success.

source: Krieglstein, Beege, Rey, Ginns, Krell and Schneider (2022) A systematic meta-analysis of the reliability and validity of subjective cognitive load questionnaires in experimental multimedia learning research
finding: Authors conclude the evidence seems to support the three-factor model, but flag that ICL-ECL overlap weakens additivity and discriminant validity. The Leppink 2013 ICL-GCL correlation was not significant, which they read as consistent with additivity.
numbers: Notes that Zu et al. (2021) found the ability to separate ICL from ECL depends on prior knowledge. Begg rank tests for publication bias non-significant.
limits: Authors are in the CLT measurement tradition.
agent_relevance: Expertise changes how load types are perceived, so agent logic keyed on load types should be conditioned on competence.

source: Jiang and Kalyuga (2020) Confirmatory factor analysis of cognitive load ratings supports a two-factor model
finding: Confirmatory factor analysis of a 12-item rating (4 items each for intrinsic, extraneous, germane) fit a two-factor model (intrinsic and extraneous) well, supporting Kalyuga's claim that germane is redundant.
numbers: N=60 first-year undergraduates, English listening task. chi2=54.069, df=53, p=.433; CFI=.994, TLI=.993, RMSEA=.018, SRMR=.077. All loadings above .30 except one item (CL11 at .28).
limits: Small N (60); one domain; reanalysis of a presentation-format experiment; no head-to-head test against the 3-factor model seen in the text I read.
agent_relevance: Supports a simple two-load design: task complexity versus wasteful presentation.

source: Jiang and Kalyuga (2020) Confirmatory factor analysis of cognitive load ratings supports a two-factor model (review of Leppink 2013 and 2014 inside the paper)
finding: Earlier 3-factor questionnaire work was only partly supportive: in two of four experiments the 3-factor solution held only partly, and germane ratings did not correlate significantly with performance.
numbers: Leppink 2013: four experiments (PCA in Exp 1 and EFA in Exp 3 supported; Exp 2 and 4 partial). Leppink 2014: two further experiments.
quote: support for the assumption that the third factor ... represents or closely relates to germane cognitive load is limited
limits: Secondhand through Jiang and Kalyuga; Leppink papers themselves not opened.

source: Sweller, van Merrienboer and Paas (2019) Cognitive architecture and instructional design: 20 years later
finding: The CLT authors answered critics. Germane load is redefined: it no longer adds its own load but redistributes working-memory resources from extraneous to intrinsic activities. Only intrinsic and extraneous are kept as basic categories.
numbers: Educ Psych Rev 31:261-292. Says the 1998 version (germane substitutes for extraneous) predicted no total change after reducing extraneous load, but many studies showed a drop in load.
quote: germane cognitive load redistributes working memory resources from extraneous activities to activities directly relevant to learning
limits: Self-correction by the theory owners; a concession to the critics, not an independent test.
agent_relevance: Treat germane as an allocation of effort, not a third load to maximise.

source: Sweller, van Merrienboer and Paas (2019) Cognitive architecture and instructional design: 20 years later
finding: Element interactivity now counts for both intrinsic and extraneous load; intrinsic load depends on the knowledge of the person, not only the material.
numbers: States that in 1998 element interactivity was seen as intrinsic only; since Sweller (2010) it is seen as determining extraneous load too. Says most instructional effects reflect extraneous load.
limits: The definition risks circularity if knowledge is not measured independently.
agent_relevance: Complexity for a model depends on what it already knows. Test tasks per model, not per task label.

source: Sweller, van Merrienboer and Paas (2019) Cognitive architecture and instructional design: 20 years later
finding: Caution against using felt effort as a learning cue: high cognitive load is an invalid cue for learning (people think it cost effort so I learned).
numbers: Offers instead explaining a solution to a peer, or generating keywords after a delay, as more valid cues.
limits: Opinion with pointers to metacognition studies.
agent_relevance: Do not let the agent treat this was hard as evidence this was right. Use external checks.

source: Shang et al. (2026) United Minds or Isolated Agents? Exploring Coordination of LLMs under Cognitive Load Theory (CoThinker)
finding: Multi-agent system designed with CLT (split intrinsic load among agents, shared memory for transactional load). Gains on reasoning-heavy tasks, losses on low-load instruction following. The authors call the CLT link a functional analogy, not a mechanism.
numbers: LiveBench with Gemini models and CommonGen-Hard. Holm-corrected paired bootstrap: Data Analysis vs IO +5.3 pp (p<.001); Reasoning vs CoT +5.1 pp (p=.001); Language vs SR +6.0 pp (p<.001); some near misses vs DMAD (p=.63, p=.16). All three Holm-significant losses are on instruction-following.
limits: Load is never measured. The high vs low intrinsic load boundary is set by task type after the fact, which is the circularity critics warn about.
agent_relevance: Task splitting helps hard tasks and costs on easy ones. A scaffold should switch off for easy items.

source: Shang et al. (2026) United Minds or Isolated Agents? Exploring Coordination of LLMs under Cognitive Load Theory (CoThinker)
finding: Ablation: components help on math for Qwen but the shared memory (TMS) hurt for newer GPT models that refuse to expose steps.
numbers: Table 4 (Math subset), TMS on+Styles on / TMS on+Styles off / TMS off+Styles on: Qwen3-30B-A3B 81.87 / 69.79 / 76.41; GPT5-Nano 55.97 / 49.02 / 62.36; GPT-OSS-20B 57.15 / 48.21 / 58.37.
limits: Small ablation on one subset; run-to-run noise not seen in the text I read.
agent_relevance: Components named after load types do not transfer across models.

source: Upadhayay, Behzadan and Karbasi (2024) Cognitive Overload Attack: prompt injection for long context
finding: Used CLT as motivation for a jailbreak. Stacking load-increasing tasks (CL1 to CL6) raised attack success on safety-trained models. Claims LLMs show cognitive overload like humans.
numbers: Forbidden Question set, total ASR: Llama-3-70B 92.67%, GPT-4 90.95%, Claude-3-Opus 99.99%, Gemini-1.5-Pro 84.05%, Gemini-1.0-Pro 75.43%. JailbreakBench: 92, 90, 97, 93 and 49%. Claude-3.5-Sonnet only 53% after redesign (CL1 to CL6 failed on it).
limits: Load is the number of stacked tasks, not measured. ASR scored by LLM judges (GPT-4, Llama-3-70B). Obfuscation could explain the result as well as overload.
agent_relevance: The analogy gives a design idea but is not a validated mechanism. Treat CLT claims for LLMs as hypotheses.

source: Adapala (2025) Cognitive Load Limits in Large Language Models: benchmarking multi-hop reasoning (ICE)
finding: Adds irrelevant text (extraneous) while keeping the task fixed. A capable model degrades linearly; weak models score 0% anyway (intrinsic floor). Length alone was not the cause.
numbers: 200 questions x 10 replications. Gemini-2.0-Flash-001: control .85, 20% saturation .82, 50% .78, 80% .72; slope -0.003 per % load (p<.001); long control .82 vs control (p=.45); residue condition .78 (p=.12, not significant). GPT-4o-0613: .65 control to .55 at 80%, slope -.002, p=.07. Llama-3-8B, Llama-3-70B, Mistral-7B: 0% in all conditions.
quote: Long Control performance was statistically indistinguishable from Control
limits: Truncation and verbosity confound (about 32% of GPT-4o outputs lacked a final answer, 12% after fixes). Only document multi-hop QA. The attentional-residue effect was not significant.
agent_relevance: Irrelevant context costs accuracy even when length is held fixed, so cut extraneous text from the agent's context.

source: Adapala (2025) Cognitive Load Limits in Large Language Models: benchmarking multi-hop reasoning (ICE)
finding: Intermediate-hop recall also falls with saturation, so part of the loss is in retrieving facts, not only in the final answer.
numbers: Gemini-2.0-Flash hop recall .90 control to .75 at 80%; GPT-4o .80 to .65. Post-hoc power .85 (Gemini) and .78 (GPT-4o).
limits: Single benchmark family (SEC filings, FanOutQA, MINTQA).
agent_relevance: Check intermediate steps, not only the final answer.

source: Mittal (2026) Did you forget what I asked? Prospective memory failures in LLMs
finding: Format constraints plus a hard task: compliance drops 2 to 21% under concurrent task load; terminal constraints drop up to 50%. A reminder restores 90 to 100%. Authors say their load order is operational, not a cognitive scale.
numbers: Over 8,000 prompts, 3 model families (o4-mini, DeepSeek-V3.1, Llama-3.3-70B), 3 runs. Mean drop: DeepSeek 10.2%, o4-mini 8.9%. Reminder average gain 17.7% (o4-mini), 16.9% (DeepSeek), 12.7% (Llama). Constraints also cost accuracy: GSM8K 93% to 27% for one model (chained).
limits: Deliberately avoids claiming a CLT mechanism; no model internals measured.
agent_relevance: Repeat key constraints at the end of the prompt. Do not stack many rules.

source: Long et al. (2025) What makes a good natural language prompt?
finding: Uses the three CLT loads as a rubric for prompts (manage intrinsic, reduce extraneous, encourage germane) across 150+ papers, mapping germane loosely to deep-thinking prompts such as ask-itself.
numbers: Meta-analysis of 150+ papers (2022-2025); 21 properties in six dimensions. Many property cells have no study.
limits: Labels are mapped onto prompt styles by analogy; no load is measured. Authors list as open whether deeper reasoning improves germane load.
agent_relevance: The labels work as design heuristics. Our schema should not claim they are measured quantities.

source: Krieglstein et al. (2022), note on Zu et al. (2021)
finding: Zu et al. (2021) reportedly found that learners separate intrinsic and extraneous load better when they have more domain knowledge.
numbers: Not read directly.
limits: Secondhand; check Zu et al. 2021 before relying.
agent_relevance: Expertise moderates how cleanly the load types separate.

source: Paas et al. (1994) / Paas, Tuovinen, Tabbers and Van Gerven (2003) as discussed by De Jong
finding: The one-item effort scale is claimed reliable, sensitive and valid; De Jong disputes the evidence base.
numbers: Not opened directly; see b05 for De Jong's reading.
limits: Secondhand.
